events.title: Earthquake / Early Warning (緊急地震速報)

alarm.title: J-Alert / Earthquake Early Warning Chime
alarm.jp_phrase: 「緊急地震速報です。強い揺れに備えてください。」
alarm.meaning: Earthquake Early Warning: Strong shaking will arrive in a few seconds to tens of seconds. Protect yourself immediately.

events.immediate_action: Drop, Cover, and Hold On. Protect your head and stay put until the shaking stops.
steps: Take shelter under a sturdy table, or protect your head and the back of your neck with a bag or cushion.
Move away from windows, bookcases that could topple, and tall furniture right away.
Do not run outside while the ground is shaking. Falling roof tiles and broken glass can seriously injure you.
When shaking stops, check and turn off gas stoves and heaters, then open a door to secure an escape route.

events.title: Tsunami Warning / Major Tsunami Warning (津波警報・大津波警報)

alarm.title: Coastal Tsunami Siren
alarm.jp_phrase: 「ウー...（長鳴3秒・休止2秒）...津波警報発令」
alarm.meaning: Tsunami Warning: A large tsunami may strike. Evacuate immediately to high ground or the upper floors of a strong building.

events.immediate_action: Move away from the coast and rivers and evacuate immediately to high ground or a Tsunami Evacuation Building (津波避難ビル).
steps: If you feel strong or long shaking near the coast, move to high ground immediately. Do not wait for a warning.
Evacuate on foot whenever possible. Cars cause traffic jams and can keep you from escaping in time.
Go to high ground or a sturdy reinforced-concrete building (3rd floor or higher), and stay there until the warning is lifted.
Tsunamis come in repeated waves. Even after the first wave has passed, do NOT go near the coast.

events.title: Emergency Broadcast: Evacuation Order (防災行政無線・避難指示)

alarm.title: Local Emergency Loudspeaker Broadcast
alarm.jp_phrase: 「緊急放送。避難指示が発令されました。」
alarm.meaning: Alert Level 4 "Evacuation Order" has been issued. All residents in the affected area must evacuate from dangerous places immediately.

events.immediate_action: Check the broadcast and start evacuating to a safe place right away, using your own judgment.
steps: If wind or rain makes the loudspeaker hard to hear, check your local government's disaster website or a disaster-prevention app.
Take your emergency bag and go to the nearest designated emergency evacuation site (指定緊急避難場所) or another safe building.
At night, or if going outside is dangerous, do not force yourself to go out. Move to a safer place inside your home, such as an upper floor or a room on the side facing away from the mountain.

events.title: Heatstroke Alert / Extreme Heat (熱中症)
events.immediate_action: Move to an air-conditioned room and replenish water and salt (electrolytes).
steps: When a Heatstroke Alert (熱中症警戒アラート) is issued, avoid unnecessary outings and outdoor exercise.
Drink water and replenish salt little by little, before you feel thirsty.
If you feel dizzy, have a headache, or feel lightheaded when standing, move to a cool, breezy place, loosen your clothing, and cool your neck and armpits.
